title: This Tree In Delhi's Dwarka Sector 9 Is 'Haunted'. Beneath Its Concrete Base Lies A Buried...
text:
This Tree In Delhi’s Dwarka Sector 9 Is ‘Haunted’. Beneath Its Concrete Base Lies A Buried...
We stumbled upon a viral video of a haunted tree in Dwarka, Delhi, which is associated with several spooky stories
The haunted tree in Dwarka is part of a circular stepwell in Delhi. (Photo Credit: Instagram) The haunted tree in Dwarka is part of a circular stepwell in Delhi. (Photo Credit: Instagram)
Haunted places around the world have always intrigued curiosity among many travel enthusiasts and history explorers. One such video, which has been amassing considerable attention on social media, features one of the haunted trees located in Dwarka Sector 9 of the national capital. A travel vlogger named Nakul Chhabra Dehlvi shared the video on Instagram featuring the haunted tree and shared common incidents related to the place.
Haunted tree in Dwarka, Delhi
Recommended Stories
In the video, Nakul Chhabra Dehlvi gave a virtual tour of the place in Dwarka Sector 9, which has the haunted tree. Alongside the video, he talked at length about the spooky incidents associated with the place.
He said, “Kehete hai raat ke time iss per ke aaspass ek ajeeb si energy mehsoos hoti hai aur isi wajah se log yahapar gujarte huye apni speed badha lete hai. Par kya yahape sachmein koi bhut hai? Ki ye kahani kuch bahut badi sachchai ko chupa rhi hai? (It is said that at night a strange energy is felt around this place and due to this people increase their speed while passing through it. But is there something really big here? Is this story hiding some big truth?)"
“Yeh actually mein ek circular baoli hai, ek purana step well jo samay ke saath niche ja chuka hai. Ye baoli ka structure alag hai, ye circular hai jo Delhi ke baaki baoliyon se kaafi different hai. Aur isi wajah se main ise kahunga yeh ek World Heritage Site hai (This is actually a circular well, an old step well which has been demolished with time. The structure of this well is different, it is circular which is quite different from the other wells of Delhi. And that is why I would call it a World Heritage Site)," he continued.
The haunted tree is also part of a historical survey
Nakul captioned the video as “What if I told you… that the “haunted tree" in Dwarka Sector 9 is actually a buried baoli? Hidden beneath layers of concrete and local legend lies a rare circular stepwell, believed to be part of Toganpur village — a name most Delhiites haven’t even heard."
He also cited a mention of the place in one of the historically significant surveys and penned, “This forgotten gem finds a quiet mention in Maulvi Zafar Hassan’s survey “Monuments of Delhi", but today, it hides in plain sight, mistaken for myth. What looks spooky… might actually be sacred."
Social media users’ reaction to the haunted tree video
The travel vlogger further leaves an open question for his viewers to share their personal experiences while crossing this place. Soon, social media users began reacting to the video.
One user, echoing the same opinion, said, “True, speed toh badh jati hai."
Another added, “Yahan ek ped hota tha kabhi bohot bada wo ab nahi hai us ped se he kuch feel hota tha hamesha."
A third person said, “This is not that tree. That tree was huge..The location is same."
“Bhoot he waha pe," said someone.
A user mentioned, “Kuch nhi..logo ne faltu baate boli hui h…" One person person wrote, “It’s a lie, I come from here everyday," while a person said, “I haven’t felt like this till now, yes, I will definitely note it."
The video was shared on May 19, and has already gained tonnes of views on Instagram.
